Your private visit notebook

The little details, together.

Yours to keep
▤

What helps a conversation?

It is easy to forget a question in the exam room. Make a simple note to bring to any veterinary visit.

  • When a change first appeared and whether it comes and goes.
  • Food, medicines and supplements currently given.
  • Photos or short videos of symptoms that are hard to show in a visit.
  • The two or three questions you most want answered.

Just in this tab. Your note stays in this browser tab. You can download it as a text file; nothing is sent to a veterinary practice.

READY TO BRING ALONG

The Kindred way

Room for a calmer hello.

A familiar blanket, a little extra time and a chance to ask questions can help you prepare. Tell your veterinary team what helps your pet feel safe.

  • ♡ A calm hello
  • ? Time for questions
  • ↗ A clear next step

Good to know

Questions are welcome.

There is no such thing as a silly question when it comes to someone you love.

What should I bring to a first visit?+

Bring any previous medical records, a list of medicines or supplements, and the questions on your mind. A familiar blanket or favourite treat can also help your pet settle.

How can I help a nervous pet feel comfortable?+

Give yourself extra time to arrive, and let your veterinary team know what tends to worry your pet. For cats and smaller companions, a secure carrier with familiar bedding is helpful.

When should I seek urgent care?+

Breathing trouble, collapse, severe injury, seizures, and suspected poisoning need prompt veterinary attention. Contact an emergency veterinary provider immediately.

Can I ask about nutrition or behaviour?+

Absolutely. Food, routines, and behaviour are part of your pet's wellbeing. Share your concerns during a visit so the team can understand the full picture.
